# dsh-armory · Armory

Chinese | [English](https://github.com/2026heshao/dsh-armory/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

> **You don't need to remember what's installed in DSH.**
> Armory brings MCP, skills, experts, plugins, and four markets into one panel: 316 connectors, 190k+ skills, and 429 experts. What's installed, what failed to connect, and which tools are consuming tokens are all visible as soon as you open it. Anything you need in a session can be called up directly.

## Install the panel

```sh
# npm (recommended, no build authorization needed)
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-armory

# From GitHub
dsh plugin --profile web add github:2026heshao/dsh-armory
```

After installing, **fully quit DSH and then restart it**. A new line, "大肥鱼军械库" (Big Fat Fish Armory), will appear under "Global panel" in the top left. Click it to open the panel. The floating button in the bottom right and the bottom of the left sidebar also open it. On desktop, replace `--profile web` with `--profile desktop`.

You can keep just one of the three entry points or enable all of them. Switch them in "Entrances" at the top right of the panel. You can't end up with all three turned off and no way to open it.

> Don't manually insert `dsh-armory` into a profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, an Agent preset, or an extra `--patch` file. The plugin command already handles this, and duplicate wiring will raise an explicit error.

## What it keeps an eye on for you

### MCP: see at a glance whether it's connected

Each MCP gets one row: status, transport, connection parameters, and tool count. Expand it to see the full input Schema, including required and optional fields, enums, and defaults. Credentials are masked by default. Click to reveal them temporarily, and click again to hide them. If a connection fails, reconnect in place without restarting the host.

Global and project scopes are managed separately. Global writes to the profile and is available in all projects. Project writes to `.dsh/mcp.json` and is visible only to sessions in that project. A project can also disable a particular global MCP without affecting other projects. Saving project config takes effect immediately for running sessions, so there's no need to reopen them.

You don't have to copy entries over one by one when migrating from other clients. Configs from 11 clients, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Gemini CLI, and Roo Code, are detected automatically. Preview and import them with one click. If names conflict, only the conflicting entry is skipped. Pasting `mcpServers` JSON also works.

For remote MCPs that require OAuth, a 401 response from the server opens the authorization dialog directly. The browser handles discovery, registration, PKCE, and the callback. The token is written back to the config, and the plugin refreshes it before it expires. If the callback isn't received, you can paste the callback URL or an access token.

# Ciallang

A TJS2 script language interpreter implemented in C++20, aimed at Kirikiri script compatibility and host embedding.
Supports Linux, macOS, and Windows.

## What it can do

- Executes TJS2 source code: functions, classes, properties, exceptions, preprocessing, variadic arguments, and common literals.
- Provides standard library capabilities for Array, Dictionary, String, Math, Date, RegExp, Exception, and Octet.
- Loads TJS2 bytecode and translates it into internal instructions for execution. For the compatibility scope, see [compatibility notes](https://github.com/2468785842/Ciallang/blob/HEAD/doc/compatibility.md).

- Embeds as a CMake subproject or as an installed SDK, registering host classes, functions, and properties through the C++ API.

Integer JIT, Trace JIT, and tail-call optimization must be explicitly enabled. For their scope, see [JIT](https://github.com/2468785842/Ciallang/blob/HEAD/doc/jit.md) and [tail recursion](https://github.com/2468785842/Ciallang/blob/HEAD/doc/tail-recursion.md).

> **⚠️ Research-stage notice**: This project is currently in **experimental R&D**. Code and features may undergo **large-scale refactoring or updates**, and releases may not keep up with the latest changes. Please **use with caution in production environments**. Verify in a test or staging environment first, and pin the versions of your dependencies.

# CTX-Audit

**Deterministic code security fact engine · PR drift gate · forensic tool surface for agents (MCP)**

Deterministically answers four questions: **Does this PR introduce security drift?**, **Who has authentication on these endpoints?**, **Is there a reachable path from entry point to sink?**, **Can a payload actually survive to reach the sink?**

It does not pursue general vulnerability discovery. Candidate chains and the fact layer are left to the LLM or a human for the final verdict. Every conclusion carries `provenance` and `uncertainty`, so it can be reviewed and falsified.

[English](https://github.com/BlkSword/CTX-Audit/blob/HEAD/README_EN.md)

---

## Table of Contents

- [Positioning](#定位)
- [Core Capabilities](#核心能力)
- [Quick Start](#快速开始)
- [PR Security Drift Gate](#pr-安全漂移闸门)

- [Architecture](#架构)
- [Development and Testing](#开发与测试)
- [License](#许可证)

## Positioning

CTX-Audit is a **fact engine**, not a vulnerability scanner:

| It does | It does not do |
|---|---|
| Enumerate endpoints and authentication coverage (declarative + middleware) | Claim "there is definitely a vulnerability here" |
| Compare base and head, and output PR drift verdicts | Full SAST / rule stacking |
| Provide entry-to-sink reachable paths and chain tiers | Execute target code (dynamic verification must be explicitly enabled) |
| Trace payload state hop by hop (killed / may_survive / taint_lost) | Complete type- and alias-aware CPG data flow |
| Output reproducible curl/MockMvc verification skeletons | Automatically generate PoCs and attack targets |

**Design principles**: zero build, sub-second, deterministic (byte-identical output across repeated runs on the same input), and every fact carries provenance and uncertainty.

ReDChicagOTypewriteR/ShotAI.body:
## Project Overview

ShotAI brings local large language models, file Q&A, a document library, image understanding, image creation, and host monitoring together into one desktop application. After an administrator installs it on a Windows or Ubuntu host and prepares the models, other users on the LAN only need to open a browser; they do not need to install model runtimes separately.

ShotAI handles the interface, model management, task routing, file processing, and LAN sharing. Ollama and the local image runtime components perform the actual inference. Model weights are not included in the installation package.

## Key Capabilities

| Capability | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Local chat | Streaming responses, stop, regenerate, edit questions, and multi-session management |
| Chinese and English interface | Switch between Chinese and English in settings; follows the system language on first launch, and falls back to English in non-Chinese environments |
| Files and library | Analyze files in chat, generate or modify Excel / Word / PDF, and search the library |
| Image understanding | Use vision models to analyze images, screenshots, and document pages |
| Image generation and editing | Describe generation requirements directly in the chat, and continue modifying the previous image |
| Model management | Import, health check, actual load detection, diagnostics, and full cleanup |
| LAN sharing | The host provides a unified `9090` entry point, and other devices use it through a browser |
| Host monitoring | View online count, task queue, CPU, memory, disk, and GPU status |

## Quick Start

Install the software package for your platform, import models on the host, then use it on a trusted LAN at `http://主机IPv4地址:9090`. The installation package does not include model weights or NVIDIA drivers. Image generation requires an optional runtime extension for the same platform.

## What can I use it for?

For example, you say:

> "Make a 5-episode Shangmeiying-style short drama about Wu Song fighting a tiger"

It will then give you five things, all in Chinese, copy-and-use ready:

| What you get | What it's for |
|----------|----------|
| ① Script | A 5-episode storyboard script, 15 seconds per episode, with storyteller narration, dialogue, and subtitle-card timing |
| ② Color palette | A color list specific to this series (e.g., 朱砂红/鎏金/墨黑/青瓷绿 = cinnabar red / gilded gold / ink black / celadon green), used throughout to prevent color drift |
| ③ Asset list | Image prompts for characters, scenes, and props; paste into 即梦/Seedream to generate images |
| ④ Per-episode storyboard | Seedance 2.0-specific prompts (timeline format); paste the whole block to generate the video |
| ⑤ Last-frame notes | A description of each episode's final frame, used by the next episode for seamless continuity |

## How to use it (three steps)

**Step 1: Describe your request in plain language.** The story can be one sentence ("make a Kuafu chasing the sun"), a novel, or a mythological allusion. Any of these works.

# dsh-hos-scrcpy

**DSH's HarmonyOS screen-casting provider**: it lets DSH connect to HarmonyOS devices through `hdc`, so you can view the screen, tap and swipe, press keys, input text, and let the AI see the display.

The UI, AI tools, device and focus handling, routing, and gating are **all in core**. This package only handles **how the device connects, how taps are sent, and how the picture is output**.

> **Maintenance note**: I have limited bandwidth lately, so maintenance and replies may be slow. I do read issues and PRs, but I can't commit to a timeline right now. Thanks for your patience.

## What is this

| | |
|---|---|
| Role | dsh-scrcpy **provider** (HarmonyOS platform) |
| Dependency | Requires **`dsh-scrcpy-core`**. Without it this package won't activate. This package **does not declare** a package dependency on core. The two packages are **installed independently** and don't pull each other in automatically |
| Transport | `hdc`: USB debugging, or wireless via `hdc tconn` |
| Sidecar | One **Java process** per device (the compiled output of `Dev/src/Main.java` ships with the package), started by this package via `spawn`: `java -cp <jar>;<out> Main --sn … --hdc … --port 0 --scale … --frame-rate … --bit-rate … --ifr … --idle-exit …` |
| Protocol | The browser side **connects directly to the sidecar's WebSocket**: binary H.264 (annex-B) plus JSON control messages (`size` / `log` / `hid`). Touch and key input share the same connection |
| Not in the stream path | The provider only starts and stops the sidecar, reports devices, and reports configuration. Video frames and touch input **do not pass through it**. This is its biggest difference from the Android provider |
| Not included | Browser side, AI tools, AI prompts, UI registration, focus logic (all in core) |

## Features

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| **Cross-platform, multi-device** | Several devices can be cast at once, each with its own independent session and tab. **Android and HarmonyOS can be displayed at the same time without conflict.** Actions only apply to the currently focused device (the visible panel), so you won't tap the wrong one |
| **Works on Huawei retail devices** | Uses the system screen-casting service path, so **no root, no system partition changes, and no allowlist** are needed |
| **Rotation** | The picture follows after rotating. **No reconnect needed and no black screen.** Rebuilding is driven only by the SPS in the stream, which is platform-independent |
| **Page switching / pausing** | Pauses automatically when you switch away. **No need to keep it running or disconnect and reconnect.** Uses very few resources while paused. The picture **appears immediately** when you switch back, because the sidecar caches the config plus the frames from the most recent keyframe onward and resends them. **Rotating the device while paused doesn't crash when you switch back** |

git clone https://github.com/qsumm/TestOPS.git && cd TestOPS

xingxingbk-git/dsh-deepseek-chat.body:
---

DeepSeek Chat is a **DSH desktop plugin**: select **CHAT** to use the real [DeepSeek Chat website](https://chat.deepseek.com/) inside DSH; select **HARNESS** to return to your original workspace at any time. The plugin does not take over your account system; website login is stored separately.

Current release **0.2.27** · For **DSH Desktop** · The CHAT web page's language, appearance, and font size follow DSH.

## Core Features

- **One-click CHAT / HARNESS switching**: Toggle beside the brand in the top-left corner; the sidebar shows the website's conversation list, pinned items, and date groups.
- **Shortcut switching**: By default, press `Tab` to toggle back and forth between the two modes; you can also customize two shortcuts.
- **Web page caching strategy**: Cache web pages, delay release, or release immediately, balancing switching speed against developer tools (F12) as you prefer.
- **Attachment download**: Code blocks, images, and common attachments can be saved to your local machine; external links are handed off to the system's default browser.
- **Appearance following**: Language, light/dark theme, and content font size follow DSH, with no need to set them again.

## How to Use It Better

The most suitable workflow for this plugin is **“talk it through first, then act”**:

1. Switch to **CHAT** and first talk through the plan clearly in the website chat (this step does not consume Harness Tokens).
2. Copy the conclusion, plan text, or share link.
3. Use the shortcut to switch back to **HARNESS**.
4. Paste the conclusion to the Agent and have it develop directly according to the confirmed plan.

Benefits of this approach:

- **Saves Tokens**: Plan discussion happens in the website chat and does not occupy Harness context.
- **Saves context**: Only the confirmed conclusion is handed to the Agent, reducing back-and-forth clarification and irrelevant history.
- **More precise**: The Agent receives a finalized plan rather than dozens of rounds of trial and error.

Two typical scenarios:

- **Requirements breakdown**: First, in CHAT, have the website model help you break down requirements and compare options; once finalized, switch back to HARNESS and develop directly.
- **Error troubleshooting**: Paste the error into CHAT to ask about the cause and fix, then bring the conclusion back to HARNESS and have the Agent modify the code.

## Quick Start

1. Install the plugin (see “Installation” below), **fully quit and reopen DSH**.
2. Switch to **CHAT**, click **Log in to DeepSeek**, and log in normally on the website page within the plugin.
3. After logging in, your account and conversation list sync automatically; **Settings → Chat Settings** lets you view the account, log out, and adjust preferences.
4. To return to your original workspace, switch to **HARNESS**; your original panel will be restored.

## Installation

### Install by name (current release)

Enter the following in the DSH plugin install input box:

```text
dsh-deepseek-chat@0.2.27
```

Or use the command line:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile…
```

zhuobichen/weflow-cli.description: A local-first WeChat data tool: chat history query and export, official account daily digest, and personal knowledge base (MCP compatible)
zhuobichen/weflow-cli.body:
**Simplified Chinese** · [English](https://github.com/zhuobichen/weflow-cli/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

*Today's people don't see the moon of ancient times; this moon once shone on the ancients.*

> For heaven and earth are the inn of all things; time is the passing guest of a hundred generations.

> Bring chat records, official account reading, and personal knowledge workflows back to your local computer.

**WeFlow CLI turns WeChat into your local second brain.** Four things, all done on your machine. It doesn't log into your account and doesn't upload chat content:

| | What you get | Where to start |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 💬 **Chat records** | Query and search by person, by group, or by time; export to HTML you can browse directly (including images and voice transcription) | `weflow-cli export` |
| 📰 **Official accounts** | Organize subscribed account articles into a daily digest with AI summaries; can be sent by email | `weflow-cli daily` |
| ⭐ **Favorites** | Read the local favorites library and search by type and keyword (articles, images, links) | `weflow-cli fav list` |
| 🧠 **Knowledge base** | Articles and chats distilled into semantically searchable notes and a concept graph | `weflow-cli search` · `weflow-cli wiki` |

Supports Windows and Linux. Has an MCP interface that can connect to AI editors such as Claude Code.

It is built to answer **a few questions WeChat itself can't answer**: who is waiting for my reply, what I promised whom and whether I did it, which relationships are fading, how a given account's views have changed, and what we were talking about on this day in past years.

> **Local-first**: Data is processed on the local machine by default, with no built-in telemetry. Online services and cloud AI that you explicitly choose will make network requests. Encryption of configured keys, the separate key cache, and the optional plaintext database cache have different security boundaries; see the [Security and Privacy Statement](https://github.com/zhuobichen/weflow-cli/blob/HEAD/SECURITY.md) for details.

> This project is limited to processing data you have access to. Please comply with applicable laws, WeChat's rules, and others' privacy boundaries.

> **⚠️ Usage boundaries and risks**: Use only on devices you control, and only with data you own or are explicitly authorized to access. Do not use this project to monitor, track, or read other people's WeChat data, and do not deploy it on others' devices or run it remotely and silently. Before use, confirm the applicable laws, WeChat's terms of service, and your account permissions yourself. Third-party tools may trigger account risk controls, restrictions, or bans. This project does not constitute legal advice; users bear responsibility for their own use.

## Overview

**WeChat favorites query** (reads the local `favorite.db`, supports type filtering and keyword search):

```text
$ weflow-cli fav list -n 3

Favorites list (1042 total, 3 shown):

[2026/8/21 19:42:42]…
```
